correctness.rationale: A crown perfect matching equals a derangement; the exact four-cycle move is a legal arbitrary-position transposition. Common relabelling acts by conjugation, so BFS from every integer-partition cycle-type representative gives all graph eccentricities. Two separately implemented exhaustive enumerators verify every matching and every BFS distance histogram for n=4 through 9, including n=9 with 133496 states, 1835568 edges, and all 8 cycle types. Exactly one class, (3,3,3), has eccentricity 10; its sole farthest vertex is the inverse. This gives 2240/2=1120 unordered antipodal pairs. Finite scope is explicit.

evidence: A matching of the crown graph is exactly a fixed-point-free permutation; a square switch is any transposition of input positions preserving that property.

originality.rationale: The exact nine-pair graph distance, first exceeding the part size, and its complete inverse-antipode classification are not stated or implied by the two primary reconfiguration sources inspected. The established diameter bound of Dyer–Jerrum–Müller is restricted to chordal bipartite graphs and cannot be applied to crowns (which contain induced six-cycles). Bonamy et al. address reconfiguration reachability and complexity, not these exact metric data. Known adjacent-position derangement swaps use a strictly smaller legal-move set. Searches did not reveal a covering theorem or table, subject to the specified unindexed-data risk.
residual_risks: A prior equivalent finite enumeration may be buried in unindexed graph-switching computations or supplementary datasets.
The 2019 manuscript was assessed through its directly relevant sections and targeted searches, not line-by-line rederived throughout its remaining text.
Scientific correctness is exhaustively checked within the specified finite domain, but has no independent external audit.

value.rationale: A crown is the simplest dense bipartite family obtained by forbidding a perfect matching. The exact first switch-diameter excess over part size supplies a meaningful sharp boundary for transferring the n-step diameter principle established for chordal bipartite graphs, while the complete inverse-antipode classification identifies an intrinsic extremal mechanism rather than merely reporting one eccentricity or a vertex count. The precise facts are natural for sampling-chain path lengths and perfect-matching reconfiguration benchmarking, without asserting any new mixing-time theorem.
